description: Blue Team Village focuses on defensive security operations, digital forensics and incident response (DFIR), multi-cloud posture, threat intelligence pivoting, Velociraptor, and Osquery detection engineering.

talks.title: Adventures in Pro Bono Digital Forensics Work
talks.teaser: John Bambenek recounts pro bono digital forensics casework, exposing flawed prosecution expert testimony and emphasizing sound forensic methodologies.
talks.summary:
The Power Imbalance in Digital Forensic Justice

In criminal and civil legal disputes, defendants lacking financial resources often cannot afford qualified digital forensics experts to challenge flawed government or prosecution evidence.

Case Studies in Pro Bono Defense Forensics

John Bambenek shares real-world cases where pro bono defense investigations uncovered sloppy forensic analysis, fabricated evidence claims, and misinterpreted log files.

Cautionary Tales of Flawed Forensic Methodologies

Bambenek reviews egregious errors in forensic investigations—including failing to verify file timestamps, misattributing IP addresses, and over-relying on automated tools.

A Call for Pro Bono Community Contributions

The author calls on experienced DFIR practitioners to volunteer their time to ensure equitable access to sound forensic expertise in the legal system.

talks.title: Threat Report Roulette: Advanced CTI & Pivoting
talks.teaser: Ch33r10 and Jorge Orchilles turn standard threat reports into actionable intelligence, demonstrating advanced TTP extraction, adversary emulation, and hunting pivots.
talks.summary:
Moving Beyond Basic Threat Intelligence Ingestion

Standard CTI workflows often stop at extracting static Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and feeding them into threat intelligence platforms (TIPs) for basic hash matching.

Deconstructing Adversary TTPs from Threat Reports

Ch33r10 and Jorge Orchilles demonstrate how to analyze newly published threat reports to extract underlying Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs).

Pivoting and Adversary Emulation Workflows

The speakers walk through creating custom adversary emulation plans in SCYTHE based on threat reports, allowing blue teams to test defenses against reported adversary behaviors.

Taking Detection Engineering to the Next Level

The authors provide incident responders with structured hunting queries and behavioral detection rules derived directly from adversary tradecraft.

talks.title: Forensicating Endpoint Artifacts in Cloud Storage Services
talks.teaser: Renzon Cruz investigates host forensic artifacts left by cloud sync clients (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox), tracing insider data exfiltration.
talks.summary:
Cloud Storage Sync Clients as an Investigation Frontier

Modern enterprise endpoints integrate desktop sync clients for OneDrive, Google Drive, Box, and Dropbox, which are frequently leveraged by insiders and adversaries for data exfiltration.

Extracting Local Cloud Client Forensic Artifacts

Renzon Cruz details forensic extraction techniques for local sync SQLite databases, sync log files, shellbags, and cache directories across Windows and macOS.

Reconstructing File Deletion and Upload Timelines

Cruz demonstrates parsing local sync telemetry to determine exact file modification timestamps, uploaded file paths, user account associations, and sync status.

DFIR Triage Workflows for Cloud Storage Intrusions

The presentation provides investigators with open-source parsers and investigative checklists to rapidly quantify exfiltrated data volumes.

talks.title: How Do You ALL THE CLOUDS: Multi-Cloud Security Strategy
talks.teaser: Henry delivers an energetic, practical guide to securing multi-cloud environments, eliminating dangling DNS, exposed storage buckets, and IAM privilege sprawl.
talks.summary:
The Chaos of Multi-Cloud Enterprise Sprawl

Managing enterprise security across AWS, Azure, and GCP requires balancing disparate security models, inconsistent logging schemas, and fragmented asset inventories.

Eliminating Critical Cloud Blind Spots

Henry reviews pervasive multi-cloud vulnerabilities—including dangling DNS records, publicly accessible object storage buckets, and unmanaged compute instances.

Establishing Unified IAM and Network Guardrails

The author explains how to implement centralized IAM auditing, enforce least-privilege role boundaries, and automate security group compliance across cloud providers.

A Pragmatic Blueprint for Cloud Defense

The presentation provides enterprise defenders with a structured roadmap for asset discovery, continuous compliance monitoring, and posture management.

talks.title: SubWatcher: Auditing Azure RBAC & Subscription Access
talks.teaser: Igal Flegmann introduces SubWatcher, an open-source tool to monitor Azure RBAC assignments, scan subscriptions, and detect unauthorized access paths.
talks.summary:
The Complexity of Azure Role-Based Access Control

In large Microsoft Azure environments, tracking effective RBAC permissions across subscriptions, resource groups, and service principals is notoriously difficult.

Introducing SubWatcher for Azure RBAC Auditing

Igal Flegmann presents SubWatcher, an open-source tool developed to continuously scan Azure subscriptions and map role assignments.

Detecting Unauthorized and Overprivileged Access

SubWatcher identifies risky access configurations, such as external guest accounts assigned Owner roles, orphaned service principals, and unauthorized role grants.

Automating Continuous Subscription Governance

Flegmann demonstrates integrating SubWatcher into CI/CD pipelines and alerting workflows to enforce least-privilege RBAC standards.

talks.title: Logjamming: Tales of Innovation, Intrigue, & Shenanigans
talks.teaser: Defenders explore unconventional log analysis techniques, correlating seemingly unrelated telemetry sources to uncover stealthy enterprise intrusions.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Security Research Presentation

This talk covers technical security topics and vulnerability research. The presentation includes discussion of contemporary security challenges, demonstrations of exploitation techniques, and insights into defensive countermeasures and security best practices.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Modern Authentication for the Security Admin
talks.teaser: Microsoft identity expert Mark Morowczynski demystifies modern authentication protocols (SAML, OAuth, OIDC, JWTs) for non-identity security administrators.
talks.summary:
The Shift from Legacy to Modern Authentication

Modern enterprise security relies on token-based authentication protocols (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML 2.0) to authenticate users and authorize API access across cloud services.

Deconstructing Authentication Flows and Claims

Mark Morowczynski breaks down token exchange flows, explaining how identity providers issue claims, bearer tokens, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs).

Analyzing Attack Vectors in Modern Identity

Morowczynski explores common identity attacks—including token theft, illicit OAuth app consent grants, and conditional access bypasses.

Defensive Architecture and Identity Hardening

The author provides security administrators with actionable best practices to enforce continuous access evaluation, restrict third-party app consent, and monitor authentication logs.

talks.title: Scope X: Hunt in the Ocean of Unknown Assets
talks.teaser: Meisam Eslahi introduces 'Scope X', a threat hunting methodology designed to discover and defend against entry points outside traditional assessment scopes.
talks.summary:
The Peril of Restrictive Scoping in Cybersecurity

Traditional security assessments focus narrowly on predefined scopes, yet adversaries routinely breach enterprise networks through unmapped shadow assets and forgotten perimeter systems.

Introducing the Scope X Threat Hunting Concept

Meisam Eslahi introduces 'Scope X'—a proactive hunting framework focused on identifying unknown unknowns across public infrastructure, supply chains, and subsidiaries.

Hunting for Unindexed Entry Points and Shadow IT

Eslahi demonstrates techniques for correlating passive DNS, TLS certificates, IP allocations, and ASN metadata to map an organization's true attack surface.

Integrating Scope X into Continuous Threat Hunting

The author provides blue teams with practical workflows to continuously expand threat hunting operations beyond rigid compliance scopes.

talks.title: Structured Analytical Techniques for Improving InfoSec
talks.teaser: Rabbit refactors CIA Structured Analytic Techniques (SAT) for cybersecurity, eliminating cognitive bias and improving incident response investigations.
talks.summary:
Cognitive Biases in Security Analysis and DFIR

Incident responders and threat intelligence analysts frequently suffer from cognitive biases—such as confirmation bias and anchoring—leading to flawed attribution and missed root causes.

Adapting CIA Structured Analytic Techniques

Rabbit refactors analytical methodologies published in the CIA's tradecraft manual for practical application in infosec investigations and OSINT research.

Applying Core Analytical Frameworks

The author demonstrates applying Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH), Devil's Advocacy, and Red Team Analysis to evaluate incident telemetry objectively.

Improving Investigative Rigor and Reporting

The presentation provides security teams with structured templates to document evidence, evaluate assumptions, and produce rigorous, defensible analytical conclusions.

talks.title: This Is What We Thought Would Happen in 2021: Meta-Analysis of Threat Forecasting
talks.teaser: Gert-Jan Bruggink conducts a meta-analysis on industry threat forecasts, evaluating the predictive accuracy of annual vendor cybersecurity predictions.
talks.summary:
The Annual Industry Ritual of Threat Predictions

At the start of every year, cybersecurity vendors publish hundreds of predictive reports forecasting emerging cyber threats and attack trends for the next 12 months.

Conducting a Meta-Analysis of Global Threat Forecasts

Gert-Jan Bruggink analyzes over 100 industry prediction reports from 2021, categorizing recurring themes, hype cycles, and vendor marketing biases.

Comparing Predictions Against Real-World 2021 Intrusions

Bruggink evaluates how well predictions matched actual high-impact cyber events (such as SolarWinds fallout, Colonial Pipeline, and ProxyLogon), revealing significant forecasting blindspots.

Building Evidence-Based Threat Modeling

The author provides intelligence leaders with rigorous frameworks to filter out vendor marketing noise and base security strategies on empirical threat data.

talks.title: Uncomfortable Networking: Simplifying Network Architecture for Security
talks.teaser: Charles Rumford challenges overly complex network security designs, showing how simplifying routing and segmentation enhances defensive posture.
talks.summary:
The Overhead of Overly Complex Network Security

Decades of layering firewall rules, complex VLANs, and middleboxes often create brittle network architectures that hinder operations without measurably increasing security.

Deconstructing 'Uncomfortable Networking'

Charles Rumford advocates for simplifying network topology and management overhead while reinforcing foundational access controls.

Pragmatic Micro-Segmentation and Identity-Based Access

Rumford explains how shifting from static IP/VLAN segmentation to identity-aware transport proxies simplifies network administration and eliminates firewall bloat.

A Blueprint for Maintainable Network Defense

The author provides network engineers with practical strategies to audit legacy rulebases, remove architectural technical debt, and build resilient network perimeters.

talks.title: Use DNS to Detect Domains Abused for Phishing
talks.teaser: Dutch Tax and Customs investigator Karl Lovink uses DNS telemetry and Splunk to detect fraudulent domains abusing agency brands for phishing in real time.
talks.summary:
Public Sector Organizations as Prime Phishing Targets

Government tax and revenue agencies face constant brand impersonation campaigns where cybercriminals launch fraudulent domains and spoofed emails to defraud citizens.

Leveraging DNS and SPF Telemetry for Proactive Detection

Karl Lovink details developing custom Splunk analytics that monitor global DNS queries and Sender Policy Framework (SPF / RFC 7208) lookups in real time.

Identifying Impersonation Domains Before Email Dispatch

Because phishing infrastructure queries the target's SPF record before launching mass email blasts, tracking SPF DNS telemetry provides an instant early-warning indicator.

Automated Takedowns and Citizen Protection

Lovink demonstrates automated response workflows that instantly blacklist newly identified phishing domains and initiate registrar takedowns.

talks.title: Velociraptor: Dig Deeper into Enterprise Endpoint Telemetry
talks.teaser: Velociraptor creator Mike Cohen demonstrates advanced enterprise endpoint forensics and live incident triage using Velociraptor Query Language (VQL).
talks.summary:
The Need for Rapid Enterprise Forensic Collection

During large-scale cyber intrusions, incident response teams need the ability to query thousands of enterprise endpoints in seconds to detect and remediate threats.

Inside the Velociraptor DFIR Architecture

Mike Cohen presents Velociraptor, an open-source endpoint visibility and digital forensics framework powered by the Velociraptor Query Language (VQL).

Executing Live Triage and Surgical Forensic Hunts

Cohen demonstrates writing custom VQL queries to collect memory artifacts, enumerate active process hollows, inspect raw MFT filesystems, and hunt across thousands of hosts.

Automated Remediation and Threat Hunting Playbooks

The author showcases how enterprise DFIR teams can automate response workflows, quarantine infected endpoints, and extract forensic timelines across global fleets.

talks.title: What Machine Learning Can and Can't Do for Security
talks.teaser: Wendy Edwards separates hype from reality in security AI, analyzing where machine learning excels in anomaly detection and where it fundamentally fails.
talks.summary:
Demystifying Machine Learning in Cybersecurity

While security marketing frequently touts artificial intelligence and machine learning as silver-bullet solutions, understanding their mathematical capabilities and limitations is critical.

Where Machine Learning Excels in Defense

Wendy Edwards reviews successful ML applications—including high-volume spam classification, binary feature clustering for malware detection, and network baseline anomaly detection.

The Inherent Limitations and Failure Modes of Security ML

Edwards explores why ML models struggle with high false-positive rates, concept drift, adversarial evasion attacks, and lack of explainability in incident response.

A Pragmatic Evaluation Guide for Security Practitioners

The presentation provides security teams with an objective framework to evaluate ML-based security products and understand their true operational value.

talks.title: Year of Mentoring: Blue Team Village's Meet-a-Mentor Turns One
talks.teaser: Blue Team Village celebrates the first anniversary of Meet-a-Mentor, sharing lessons learned and stories from mentor-mentee matches in defensive cybersecurity.
talks.summary:
Celebrating One Year of Community Mentorship

Blue Team Village launched the Meet-a-Mentor program to bridge the talent gap and provide structured guidance for individuals pursuing careers in defensive security.

Key Lessons from the Inaugural Year

muteki reviews the growth and operational milestones of the program, analyzing what makes mentor-mentee partnerships successful in technical domains.

First-Hand Experiences from Mentors and Mentees

Three mentor-mentee pairs share their personal journeys, discussing career transitions, resume auditing, technical interview prep, and skill development.

Expanding Community Career Pathways

The presentation invites defensive security professionals to participate as mentors and outlines future initiatives for the Blue Team Village community.

talks.title: Yeet the Leet with Osquery: Complementing EDR Telemetry
talks.teaser: Sebastian Provost demonstrates using Osquery to complement EDR/XDR systems, writing SQL queries to detect open-source C2 implant payloads on endpoints.
talks.summary:
Enhancing Endpoint Visibility with Osquery

While commercial EDR and XDR solutions provide real-time behavioral alerts, Osquery exposes an operating system as a high-performance relational database for custom querying.

Introducing Osquery for Defensive Telemetry

Sebastian Provost explains how Osquery tables represent system state—including running processes, open network sockets, loaded kernel modules, and browser extensions.

Detecting Open-Source C2 Implants with SQL Queries

Provost analyzes multiple open-source C2 frameworks (such as Mythic and Covenant), demonstrating SQL queries that detect their unique memory and disk artifacts.

Building an Open-Source Endpoint Telemetry Pipeline

The author provides defensive teams with deployment configurations and scheduled query packs to integrate Osquery into centralized threat hunting pipelines.

talks.title: Leveraging NGFWs for Threat Hunting
talks.teaser: Drimacus presents research on operating passive Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs) alongside existing detection stacks to enhance network threat hunting and visibility.
talks.summary:
Operational Value of Next-Generation Firewalls

While Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs) are traditionally deployed inline for perimeter enforcement, running passive instances provides unique visibility for defensive hunting without risking production traffic interruption.

Overcoming Application Identification Risks

Drimacus shares lessons learned from deploying passive NGFWs in enterprise environments, exploring how deep packet inspection and layer-7 application identification expose covert adversary traffic.

Practical Threat Hunting Workflows

The speaker details concrete detection queries and hunting methodology, demonstrating how blue teams can correlate NGFW flow metadata with endpoint telemetry to uncover anomalous command-and-control activity.
